//packageManager: The single source of truth for which pnpm runs anywhere: corepack reads this
field, so local shells, CI (pnpm/action-setup resolves it) and the Docker
images all get the same version without three places to keep in sync.
It is not cosmetic. pnpm-workspace.yaml carries 23 security `overrides`, and
only pnpm >=10 reads overrides from that file — pnpm 9 reads them from this
package.json's `pnpm.overrides`, sees none, compares against the 23 recorded
in pnpm-lock.yaml and aborts with ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH. All three
Dockerfiles pinned `corepack prepare pnpm@9`, so every image build failed at
the install step — verified by building them. engines.pnpm is raised to >=10
to match, since >=9 advertised a version that cannot install this workspace.
Pinned to 10.x rather than the 11.x a developer may have locally: pnpm 11
requires Node >=22.13 and every image is node:20-alpine, so 11 aborts with
supports Node >=18.12, reads the workspace overrides, and speaks the same
lockfileVersion 9.0 already committed. Bumping the runtime to Node 22 is a
separate decision that needs its own testing, not a side effect of this fix.
